newsitem.title: USA: CME lumber ends higher on mill closing talk.
newsitem.headline: CME lumber ends higher on mill closing talk.

text.p: Talk that mills will extend their seasonal down-time due to weak cash markets added to recent support from bullish U.S. housing start figures to lift CME lumber futures sharply higher late, traders said.

Futures had been drifting higher during the day after early profit taking failed to attract follow through selling interest. The market has risen sharply since Tuesday's bullish November U.S. housing starts report and offset selling interest from declining cash prices, they said.
Randon Lengths officially quoted cash spruce at $383 per tbf, off $15 from last Friday and $24 under last Wednesday.

The housing report was exceptionally bullish as it also cited increased building permits which points to continued strong home building into next year. With mills likely to extend down time, it could add to tight lumber supplies after the first of the year, they said.

Unwinding of recent bear spreads added to the gain in January. March had recently risen from $18 per tbf under to $1.70 over and profit taking on the spread turned January back over March, they added.
Lumber closed up $7.10 to $2.00 per tbf with January up most at $397.10 and March up $3.20 at $394.90 per tbf.
